title: Protocell formation on micrometeorites
task: Characterize lipid self-assembly on extraterrestrial micrometeorite surfaces
key_results: Lipids autonomously form spherical compartments and nanotubes on micrometeorite surfaces preferentially compared to sand particles; lipid nanotubes extend from particles and connect environmental objects.
comments: While the surface energy-driven mechanism is plausible for prebiotic chemistry, the relevance to actual early Earth conditions and competitive pathways remains speculative.

model_io.model: Lipid self-assembly on micrometeorite surfaces

hypotheses.hypothesis: Micrometeorite surfaces favor lipid compartmentalization more than natural sand of similar composition
hypotheses.result: Certain lipid compositions preferentially formed compartments on micrometeorites; surface energy, texture, and elemental composition contribute to differences

title: Adaptive low-rank variational quantum algorithm for simulating dissipative dynamics in photosynthetic complexes
task: Simulate open quantum dynamics in photosynthetic antenna complexes with polynomial scaling
key_results: Adaptive low-rank VQA achieves polynomial O(n^2.5Rd) scaling vs exponential O(4^n) for classical methods; fidelity 0.87–0.95 for FMO complexes (5–12 chromophores); computational crossover at N=14 chromophores; 3% agreement with experimental energy transfer timescales.
comments: The NISQ device implementation is promising but the claimed 'quantum advantage' is contingent on scaling beyond ~15 chromophores where classical methods remain practical for many biophysical questions.

model_io.model: Low-rank variational quantum algorithm (LR-VQA)
Classical benchmark methods

hypotheses.hypothesis: Singular value decomposition tensor compression enables tractable quantum simulation of photosynthetic complexes on NISQ devices
hypotheses.result: LR-VQA demonstrated fidelity 0.932±0.001 for 7-site FMO complex with realistic IBM Heron noise

hypotheses.hypothesis: Computational crossover point exists beyond which quantum methods outpace classical approaches
hypotheses.result: Crossover occurs at N=14 chromophores; LR-VQA remains sole quantum-hardware-compatible pathway for larger systems

title: Fluorescent probes as markers of cell envelope structure and function in halophilic archaea
task: Evaluate fluorescent probe compatibility with halophilic archaeal cell envelopes under extreme conditions
key_results: Six fluorescent markers tested on Halobacterium salinarum and Haloferax volcanii; propidium iodide showed unreliable behavior with false-positive dead-cell labeling; probe efficacy depends critically on growth phase, medium composition, and exposure time.
comments: The findings are valuable for extremophile microbiology but lack quantitative kinetic data on probe permeation rates or equilibration timescales under hyperhaline conditions.

model_io.model: Halophilic archaeal cell envelope with fluorescent probes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Standard fluorescent probes designed for mesophiles are incompatible with hyperhaline archaeal physiology
hypotheses.result: Propidium iodide behavior unreliable; probe utility varies by growth phase and medium composition; extended exposure times required

title: Why extensile and contractile tissues could be hard to tell apart
task: Determine whether cell shape and flow correlations can distinguish extensile from contractile active stress in epithelia
key_results: Cell shape–flow correlations (in channels, near defects, at boundaries) cannot unambiguously determine active stress type; simultaneous stress and shape measurements are necessary.
comments: The theoretical result highlights a fundamental identifiability problem in active matter inference, though the practical implications for existing experimental datasets remain unclear.

model_io.model: Continuum active nematic theory with dual tensor order parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell shape and flow patterns alone suffice to determine whether epithelial active stress is extensile or contractile
hypotheses.result: Hypothesis rejected; correlations in channels, defect zones, and boundaries remain ambiguous without direct stress measurement

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics-based drug screening platform for focal cortical dysplasia
task: Integrate single-nucleus transcriptomics with compound screening to identify seizure-reducing drugs for focal cortical dysplasia
key_results: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of 49 human FCD specimens (I-III) reveals prominent vascular dysfunction signatures in endothelial and smooth muscle cells; astrocyte transcriptional alterations across subtypes; Connectivity Map integration prioritized 20 compounds; four candidates (Betamethasone, Lodamin, Valproxam, Licochalcone A) reduced seizure-like activity in vivo
comments: Establishes transcriptome-guided screening framework linking multicellular signatures to therapeutics; vascular convergence across FCD subtypes suggests shared pathogenic mechanism; functional validation in mTOR-driven model strengthens candidates.

model_io.model: human FCD cortical specimens, in vitro seizure model, mTOR-driven FCD mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vascular dysfunction converges across FCD subtypes as shared pathogenic feature
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; endothelial and smooth muscle cell dysfunction signatures consistently observed across FCDI-III

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transcriptome-guided screening identifies seizure-reducing compounds
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; four prioritized compounds reduce seizure-like activity in vivo with efficacy correlating with transcriptomic signatures

title: Inhibiting CXCL12/CXCR4 axis enhances T cell activity in gastric cancer
task: Define CXCL12/CXCR4 axis in CAF-TAM communication and immune evasion in gastric cancer
key_results: Single-cell transcriptomics reveal increased M2-polarized TAM population in GC; CAFs induce M2 polarization via CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling; CXCR4 silencing reduces M2 macrophages and PD-L1 expression; enhanced T cell proliferation and slower tumor growth upon CXCR4 inhibition
comments: Integrates CAF-TAM communication with T cell suppression via PD-L1; CXCL12/CXCR4 axis emerges as convergence point for immune evasion; combines single-cell resolution with functional validation.

model_io.model: murine GC model, primary and immortalized CAFs, TAMs

hypotheses.hypothesis: CXCL12/CXCR4 axis mediates CAF-induced M2 macrophage polarization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; in vitro experiments demonstrate CAF-CXCL12-mediated M2 polarization reversible by CXCR4 blockade

hypotheses.hypothesis: CXCR4 inhibition enhances T cell activation and anti-tumor immunity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CXCR4 silencing reduces M2 macrophages and PD-L1, improving T cell proliferation and tumor control

title: K-Ras controls asymmetric cell divisions from the primary cilium
task: Elucidate K-Ras4B role in primary cilium-dependent asymmetric differentiation
key_results: K-Ras4B localizes to primary cilium via PDE6D; ciliary K-Ras4B (not N/H-Ras) sustains ciliation and restricts myogenic commitment during asymmetric divisions; oncogenic K-Ras4B-G12C disrupts normal differentiation; zebrafish morphology shows ciliation-dependent heart-looping defects
comments: Reveals isoform-specific subcellular signaling compartmentalization and provides mechanistic link between RASopathies and ciliopathies; B-Raf/MEK/ERK localization at cilium base suggests localized signaling control.

model_io.model: skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells and zebrafish embryos

hypotheses.hypothesis: K-Ras4B sustains ciliation to restrict myogenic commitment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; K-Ras4B abundance correlates with ciliation and blocks differentiation during asymmetric divisions

hypotheses.hypothesis: K-Ras4B isoform specificity depends on ciliary localization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cilium-restricted K-Ras4B mutant phenocopies wild-type function; N/H-Ras cannot substitute

title: ENO2 sustains cancer stemness and metastatic competence through a phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent metabolic axis in triple-negative breast cancer
task: Define ENO2-driven metabolic axis sustaining cancer stemness and metastasis in TNBC
key_results: ENO2 depletion reduces aerobic glycolysis, OXPHOS, migration, CSC frequency, and pulmonary metastasis; exogenous PEP/pyruvate restores CSC traits; ENO2 catalytic activity required for metastatic phenotype; PKM2-PEP-pyruvate axis drives CSC regulation; POMHEX inhibition phenocopies genetic loss
comments: Integrates metabolic reprogramming with stemness and metastatic competence; PEP-PKM2-pyruvate axis provides mechanistic insight but residual rescue despite PKM2 perturbation indicates additional PKM2-independent mechanisms.

model_io.model: TNBC cell lines and orthotopic xenograft models

hypotheses.hypothesis: ENO2 catalytic activity sustains CSC properties through PEP-dependent metabolic axis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; catalytically impaired ENO2 mutant fails to restore CSC traits despite expression

hypotheses.hypothesis: PEP-PKM2-pyruvate axis drives ENO2-mediated CSC maintenance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PKM2 depletion partially attenuates PEP rescue but residual effects suggest additional mechanisms

title: Role of the trophoblastic BMP7-TGM2 axis in the pathogenesis and prevention of preeclampsia
task: Define BMP7-TGM2 axis in trophoblast invasion and preeclampsia pathogenesis
key_results: Single-cell transcriptomics reveal BMP7 downregulation and TGM2 upregulation in PE; BMP7 suppresses TGM2 via ALK2/3-SMAD1/5/9-SMAD4 pathway to promote trophoblast migration/invasion; TGM2 impairs trophoblast differentiation in organoid models; recombinant BMP7 ameliorates PE-like symptoms in Ad sFlt-1 mouse model
comments: Identifies trophoblast-specific mechanistic axis relevant to shallow invasion in PE; in vivo protection likely involves BMP7 mechanisms beyond TGM2 suppression alone; BMP7 therapeutic translation warrants safety profiling.

model_io.model: human placental tissue (single-cell transcriptomics), immortalized and primary human trophoblasts, trophoblast organoids, Ad sFlt-1-induced PE mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: BMP7 suppresses TGM2 to promote trophoblast invasion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BMP7 treatment reduces TGM2 and enhances migration/invasion in functional assays

hypotheses.hypothesis: BMP7 ameliorates PE-like symptoms in vivo
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; recombinant BMP7 administration reduces Tgm2 upregulation and PE phenotypes in mouse model

title: Intrinsic polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis capacity dictates ferroptosis sensitivity under restricted arachidonic acid availability
task: Define PUFA biosynthetic capacity as ferroptosis sensitivity determinant under AA restriction
key_results: H1299 (KEAP1 WT) cells with impaired PUFA biosynthesis require exogenous AA for ferroptosis sensitivity; A549 (KEAP1 mutant) cells retain sensitivity via endogenous PUFA synthesis; FADS2 inhibition or ELOVL5 deletion phenocopies AA restriction resistance
comments: Reveals metabolic context-dependence of ferroptosis; findings suggest cell-intrinsic biosynthetic capacity should inform ferroptosis-based therapies; physiological relevance of B27 supplement conditions warrants validation.

model_io.model: human lung adenocarcinoma cell lines (H1299, A549)

hypotheses.hypothesis: PUFA biosynthetic capacity dictates ferroptosis sensitivity under AA limitation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cells with high endogenous PUFA synthesis retain sensitivity despite AA restriction

hypotheses.hypothesis: KEAP1 status influences ferroptosis dependency on exogenous AA
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; KEAP1 mutation correlates with elevated endogenous PUFA biosynthesis and ferroptosis resistance under AA limitation

title: Super-resolution atlas of SARS-CoV-2 infection reveals protease-dependent organelle maturation, dsRNA landscapes, and intracellular structural proteins
task: Map spatiotemporal organization of SARS-CoV-2 replication complexes and viral assembly
key_results: Super-resolution imaging reveals nsp5 (3CLpro) localizes within DMV lumen near pores; nsp7-nsp16 positioned interior to nsp4, supporting protease-dependent maturation; dsRNA connectors bridge DMVs and nsp3/4-lacking granules; M- and S-positive assembly intermediates localize along secretory route; nirmatrelvir induces multilayered polyprotein aggregates (nsp4-5-10-16) persisting after washout
comments: Comprehensive spatial atlas provides mechanistic framework for viral replication; protease-dependent maturation model integrated with dsRNA condensate trafficking; drug-induced reservoir state suggests antiviral escape mechanism relevant to clinical rebound.

model_io.model: SARS-CoV-2-infected human cells with super-resolution microscopy
inputs: viral RNA, non-structural proteins (nsp3-5, nsp7-16), structural proteins (M, S)

hypotheses.hypothesis: nsp5 protease-dependent maturation completes intravesicular polyprotein processing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nsp5 positioning within DMV lumen consistent with sequential processing model

hypotheses.hypothesis: dsRNA condensates mediate trafficking of replication intermediates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dsRNA connectors bridge DMVs and non-canonical granules decorated with replicase components

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nirmatrelvir induces viral drug-resistance reservoir state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; uncleaved polyprotein multilayered bodies persist after nirmatrelvir washout and precede rapid viral rebound

title: Colorectal cancer co-opts an epidermal wound healing program during metastasis to generate disseminated tumor cells
task: Define cellular states enabling colorectal cancer metastatic dissemination
key_results: DTCs transiently express wound-healing keratins (KRT17+) with reduced EZH2 activity and activated YAP; KRT17+ cells localize to invasive front of primary tumors; state is reversible upon metastatic colonization
comments: Reveals unexpected lineage plasticity and identifies a potentially therapeutic window in the transient pre-metastatic phenotype; mechanistic link between EZH2-YAP warrants functional validation.

model_io.model: patient-derived CRC organoids with serial orthotopic transplantation

hypotheses.hypothesis: DTCs adopt epidermal wound-healing program during metastatic dissemination
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; KRT17+ expression increases in DTCs before outgrowth and decreases upon colonization

hypotheses.hypothesis: EZH2 suppression and YAP activation drive wound-healing transition
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; reduced EZH2 activity and elevated YAP signaling correlate with KRT17+ state

title: Simulated microgravity with physiological shear reveals endothelial disruption in a dual-stimulus bioreactor
task: Model endothelial dysfunction under combined microgravity and shear stress
key_results: 16 h simulated microgravity with physiological shear (3 dyn/cm²) causes HUVEC cytoskeletal disorganization, VE-cadherin junction loss, and altered angiogenic factor secretion (Angpt-2, VEGF, PDGF)
comments: Addresses physiologically relevant dual-stimulus conditions absent from prior microgravity models; standardized platform enables mechanistic study but causality between cytoskeletal and junction defects remains unresolved.

model_io.model: benchtop bioreactor with HUVECs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microgravity disrupts mechanical cues critical to endothelial homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; combined microgravity-shear causes junction disorganization and cytoskeletal remodeling

title: Comprehensive analysis of miRNA expression, secretion profile, and functional network during myogenesis in response to spaceflight
task: Characterize skeletal muscle-derived miRNA expression and secretion during spaceflight-induced atrophy
key_results: Comprehensive miRNA profiling during myogenesis reveals deregulation in response to spaceflight; secretion varies by miRNA with RBP modulation suggested as regulatory mechanism; validated miRNAs linked to target gene expression and myoblast proliferation/differentiation; muscle atrophy signature identified as candidate biomarkers
comments: Demonstrates miRNA involvement in spaceflight-induced muscle atrophy; secretory component implicates systemic effects on nervous and skeletal systems; causality between specific miRNA dysregulation and atrophy phenotypes requires functional validation.

model_io.model: mouse myoblasts during differentiation and disuse-induced atrophy model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spaceflight deregulates skeletal muscle-derived miRNAs involved in atrophy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; specific miRNAs dysregulated during myogenesis in spaceflight conditions and replicated in disuse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spaceflight modulates miRNA secretion via RBP regulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; analysis suggests RBP-mediated control of miRNA secretion and retention

title: GATA1 silencing restrains granulosa cell ferroptosis through downregulation of TFRC in polycystic ovary syndrome
task: Define GATA1-TFRC axis in granulosa cell ferroptosis during PCOS pathogenesis
key_results: GATA1 elevated in PCOS mouse ovaries; GATA1 overexpression increases lipid ROS, malondialdehyde, and iron while reducing glutathione in KGN cells; GATA1 binds TFRC promoter to enhance transcription; ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 mitigates GATA1 effects; TFRC overexpression counteracts GATA1 knockdown protection
comments: Establishes GATA1-TFRC regulatory axis as PCOS mechanism; ferroptosis as pathogenic cell death driver in granulosa cells provides therapeutic angle; clinical translation requires in vivo validation of ferroptosis inhibitor efficacy.

hypotheses.hypothesis: GATA1 promotes granulosa cell ferroptosis via TFRC-mediated iron uptake
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GATA1 directly activates TFRC transcription and iron overload correlates with ferroptotic phenotype

hypotheses.hypothesis: GATA1 upregulation contributes to PCOS granulosa cell dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; elevated GATA1 in PCOS ovaries correlates with ferroptotic stress markers

title: Extracellular vesicles from inflammatory-primed stromal cells reduce in vitro inflammation in Sandhoff disease model
task: Evaluate MSC-derived extracellular vesicles from inflammatory-primed cells as neuroinflammation adjunct in Sandhoff disease
key_results: IFEVs reduce SD neuroinflammation by lowering IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β in neuronal-glial cultures; NF-κB/p65 and NLRP3 components downregulated with arginase 1 upregulation; in peripheral blood, IFEVs increase regulatory T cell proportion without cytotoxicity
comments: Establishes MSC-EV anti-inflammatory efficacy in lysosomal storage disease model; in vitro findings suggest potential to complement enzyme-restoring therapies; in vivo efficacy and biodistribution remain to be demonstrated.

model_io.model: feline and mouse Sandhoff disease models; in vitro neuronal-glial culture and PBMC cultures

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFEVs from inflammatory-primed MSCs reduce neuroinflammation in SD models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; IFEVs decrease pro-inflammatory cytokine production and NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFEVs increase regulatory T cell populations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Treg proportion increases without cytotoxic effects on T-effector cells

title: Aurora kinase A is a synthetic lethal target in FANCA-deficient cancers
task: Identify synthetic lethal dependency in FANCA-deficient cancers
key_results: AURKA is reproducible synthetic lethal target; FANCA deficiency elevates AURKA expression; AURKA inhibition induces chromosomal instability and micronucleation; FANCA most frequently altered Fanconi anemia gene across 650,000+ sequenced tumors
comments: Genome-wide CRISPR/drug screen integration validates therapeutic target; large-scale genomics support clinical translation; mechanistic basis (elevated AURKA in FANCA-deficient background) remains partially unexplored.

model_io.model: isogenic FANCA-deficient and wild-type cancer cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: FANCA deficiency creates synthetic lethal dependency on AURKA

hypotheses.hypothesis: FANCA-deficient tumors exhibit elevated genomic instability and mutational burden
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; large-scale genomics analysis supports correlation

title: ATP6AP2 in osteoblasts couples cortical bone matrix remodeling to osteocyte maturation via MMP14 activation in mice
task: Define ATP6AP2-MMP14 axis in osteocyte maturation and cortical bone organization
key_results: ATP6AP2 deletion in osteoblast lineage impairs osteocyte maturation and survival, causing irregular woven bone; ATP6AP2 promotes MMP14 surface localization in immature osteocytes; MMP14 reconstitution partially restores lamellar bone structure
comments: Identifies previously uncharacterized functions for ATP6AP2 beyond its known roles in V-ATPase assembly; woven-to-lamellar transition mechanism provides insight into bone quality determinants.

model_io.model: transgenic mice (Atp6ap2OCN-Cre) and isolated osteoblast lineage cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATP6AP2 regulates osteocyte maturation through MMP14 activation

title: Contribution of cohesins STAG1 and STAG2 to preimplantation development in mice
task: Define functional specificities of cohesin variants STAG1 and STAG2 in preimplantation development
key_results: STAG1 maternally supplied and persists beyond 2-cell stage; STAG2 accumulates via zygotic transcription; both variants dispensable individually if other present; STAG2 absence increases zygotic DNA damage and alters blastocyst transcription; early-stage alterations may contribute to mid-gestation lethality
comments: Establishes functional redundancy in preimplantation stages but reveals STAG2-specific roles in DNA damage response and transcription; persistence of defects suggests cumulative effects through later development.

hypotheses.hypothesis: STAG1 and STAG2 display functional redundancy in preimplantation viability

hypotheses.hypothesis: STAG2 has specific roles in DNA damage response and transcription
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; STAG2 absence increases zygotic DNA damage and alters blastocyst transcription patterns

title: Oxidative base damage to telomeres sensitizes cancer cells to ATR inhibition
task: Enhance ATR inhibitor efficacy in cancer via telomeric oxidative damage

hypotheses.hypothesis: Telomeric oxidative damage sensitizes cancer cells to G2/M checkpoint inhibition

hypotheses.hypothesis: Insufficient RPA at damaged telomeres drives unscheduled S-phase progression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; RPA levels directly correlate with telomere damage persistence and mitotic duration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integration of WGS breakpoints improves detection of inversion-spanning transcripts

title: Real-time estimation of pathogen transmission dynamics from wastewater

comments: Important milestone for quantum networks; heterogeneous integration of two different quantum systems without spectral tuning.

model_io.model: Hybrid light-matter interface: InAsP/InP nanowire QD + erbium-doped fiber quantum memory
inputs: single photon from QD at 980 nm

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spectral tuning required for QD-fiber matching
hypotheses.result: Refuted—natural resonance alignment eliminates tuning requirement

title: Adiabatic preparation of thermal states and entropy-noise relation on noisy quantum computers
task: Prepare thermal Gibbs states on noisy quantum computers via adiabatic evolution with entropy benchmarking
key_results: Entropy density conserved during adiabatic evolution (thermodynamic limit); depolarizing noise resilient—measured energy-temperature curve insensitive to noise amplitude; tested on Quantinuum H1-1: entropy 0.166±0.0045 per site, temperature 2.56±0.26 for 5×4 Ising model
comments: Noise-resilience surprising for depolarizing errors; entropy-noise relation provides valuable hardware benchmark metric.

model_io.model: Adiabatic Gibbs state preparation on Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion device

hypotheses.hypothesis: Depolarizing noise significantly corrupts thermal state preparation
hypotheses.result: Partially refuted—energy-temperature curve remarkably robust despite noise

title: Direct evidence of light-induced phase-fluctuations in cuprates via time-resolved ARPES
task: Probe light-induced phase fluctuations in cuprate superconductors via time-resolved ARPES
key_results: Phase fluctuations dominate non-thermal superconducting-to-normal transition in optimally-doped Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ; ultrafast tracking of phase-sensitive hybridization gap confirms direct order-parameter phase modulation
comments: Novel time-resolved probe of phase fluctuations with momentum resolution; however, limited to single material and single doping level.

model_io.model: Time-resolved and temperature-dependent ARPES on Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ

hypotheses.hypothesis: Density wave order or pair-breaking dominates light-induced transition
hypotheses.result: Refuted—phase fluctuations confirmed as primary mechanism

title: Fermi surface topology of the topological nodal-loop semimetal HfP2
task: Map Fermi surface topology of topological nodal-loop semimetal HfP₂
key_results: Two electron pockets and one hole pocket identified; Shubnikov-de Haas beating patterns observed; Berry phase nontriviality confirmed via Landau fan; transport consistent with Dirac band dispersion
comments: Systematic high-field transport characterization but indirect evidence of nodal loops; direct ARPES measurement would strengthen topology claims.

model_io.model: HfP₂ single crystal under high magnetic field (up to 34.6 T)

hypotheses.hypothesis: HfP₂ is a trivial semimetal with parabolic band structure
hypotheses.result: Refuted—nontrivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion confirmed

title: Design, fabrication and testing of an optimized single-axis MEMS capacitive accelerometer using wet etching for improved noise stability
task: Design MEMS capacitive accelerometer using wet etching with improved noise performance
key_results: Noise 18 µg/√Hz, resonance 3620 Hz, nonlinearity <0.9%, cross-axis <0.03%, dynamic range ±10 g, shock tolerance 5000 g; tunable to ±2–±200 g via beam thickness
comments: Practical cost-effective design with competitive performance; wet etching simplification trades some design flexibility vs. complex DRIE approaches.

model_io.model: Single-axis MEMS capacitive accelerometer (proof mass + suspension beams)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Enlarged proof mass and simplified architecture reduce noise while maintaining linearity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—noise floor achieved without sacrificing linearity (<0.9%)

title: A quantum magneto-photo-thermoelastic model for wave propagation in laser-excited semiconductors
task: Model quantum-modified wave propagation in laser-excited semiconductors under magnetic field
key_results: Magnetic field induces wave attenuation and phase modification via Lorentz damping; quantum diffusion smooths carrier gradients; coupled effects improve stability and enable controlled propagation in silicon
comments: Theoretical framework generalizing photo-thermoelasticity; quantum density-gradient approach provides nonlocal carrier transport.

model_io.model: Quantum magneto-photo-thermoelastic semiconductor model for silicon

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum effects negligible in laser-excited semiconductors
hypotheses.result: Refuted—quantum diffusion significantly modifies carrier spatial distribution

title: Experimental and computational evaluation of surface geometry effects on underwater acoustic beam shaping with piezoelectric transducers
task: Characterize underwater acoustic beam shaping via piezoelectric transducer geometry
key_results: Circular piston superior for large apertures (ECD > λ/2); geometry effect negligible for ECD < λ/2; circular provides narrower main lobe and lower side lobes
comments: Well-validated with FEA and experiment for circular case only; theoretical predictions for other geometries lack experimental confirmation.

model_io.model: Piston-type ultrasonic transducers (circular, square, hexagonal, octagonal)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transducer geometry significantly affects beam shaping across all aperture ranges
hypotheses.result: Partially refuted—negligible effect for ECD < λ/2; pronounced differences only at larger apertures

title: Thermal sensitivity and supply scaling effects on 7 nm FinFET based triple tail dynamic CMOS comparator for automotive/aerospace/electronics industrial applications
task: Characterize thermal and supply voltage scaling of 7 nm FinFET dynamic voltage comparator
key_results: Thermal inversion behavior—propagation delay decreases with rising temperature (opposite bulk CMOS); operates −20 to +80 °C; suitable for cryogenic and SAR ADC applications
comments: Counterintuitive thermal response offers advantage for cryogenic operation; FinFET quantum-well effects dominate at 7 nm.

model_io.model: Triple-tail FinFET CMOS comparator (7 nm process) with capacitive over-neutralization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thermal sensitivity similar to bulk CMOS—delay increases with temperature
hypotheses.result: Refuted—thermal inversion observed due to 7 nm FinFET quantum effects

title: Molecular-level freezing and melting dynamics of aqueous lithium chloride solutions using in-situ Raman spectroscopy
task: Characterize ion-specific effects on water dynamics during freezing/melting of LiCl solutions
key_results: Chain-like Li+/Cl− aggregation observed at low T in liquid phase; HOH bending band disappears with increasing concentration; 1.5 M solution shows two-step structural transformation; freezing point depression confirmed
comments: Spectroscopic insight into ion hydration but limited mechanistic understanding of chain formation and phase transition kinetics.

model_io.model: LiCl aqueous solution system with temperature cycling
outputs: Raman spectra (OH stretch, HOH bend, lattice modes)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ion concentration and temperature uniformly suppress water hydrogen bonding
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed—HOH band disappearance indicates structural change but chain aggregation shows complex ion behavior
